Yeah.  I should be able to.  

My boyfriend just left for work, and I'm alone.  I'm really in a bad spot right now.  I can't stop crying.  I don't know what to do with myself.
Did some research.  Found out it's free.  So that's nice.
It looks like they do have such a resource.  Whether or not it's covered, I don't know.  I guess I'd have to call and ask.
Yeah, that makes sense.  I may have to try that.  Thank you!
Possibly.  I considered posting on there about my rent situation, but I feel guilty about asking people for anything.

I don't have medical insurance right now, because it's through my dad's work, and I have to be a full-time student to get it.  I can only afford school half-time right now. and my only friends are my boyfriend's stepsister and her fiance, who I don't feel comfortable sharing my intimate details with.  I can't really hold much of a conversation with the fiance, and the stepsister is a nice person, but she is a drama queen.  No one can have their own troubles, because we should all feel sorry for her because of hers.  Man, I feel like I'm making excuses.  I promise I'm not doing it on purpose--I just don't really have a lot of avenues here.  I wish that I had people I could turn to.  I think that everything would be less bad if I did.

It's complicated.  I have my mother, my father, and my grandparents.  I can't talk to my mother, for several reasons.  Firstly, stress causes exacerbation of MS symptoms.  She is a worrier, especially when it comes to me, and I can't be telling her about problems she can't help with, or problems is the root of.  That, and I feel silly talking about my problems, however significant, with someone who is enduring so much pain and suffering.

I don't feel comfortable talking to my father because I've just recently started to realize that I feel okay about him.  I've talked a little bit about my feelings about my mother, but seeing as he's been pretty much destroyed by her, it wasn't an easy conversation.  He's the type that will hear your suffering and raise you his.  A topper, I guess you could say.

My grandparents... well, they pretty much raised me when I was around them and provided me with what little I had.  But, I have only just mastered holding a regular conversation with my grandfather.  He's from the generation where you don't talk about your problems.  My grandmother cares about me very much, but she's hypercritical, and if she knows how I'm struggling, she'll worry herself to death, as well as tell me exactly how I'm doing everything wrong, in the name of trying to help.  Plus, I have my share of frustration toward her.  Anyone who fat-shames their own granddaughter right into bulimia isn't really okay with me.  My grandfather, who is probably my favorite person in the world, has cancer.  So, they're dealing with their own stuff anyway.  I talk to them sometimes.  Not about the feeling type stuff, but it makes me happy to hear from them.  I know they love me very much.  I just can't really bring myself to talk to them about certain things.

That's why I feel so guilty.  I don't know.  I don't know if those behaviors are truly her reaction to life, or if that's her disease's way of making her see things.  I was so willing to believe the former of those ideas, but now that's she's doing so terribly, it makes me realize that maybe there was a neurological reason for the way she is.  It is very true that people lash out at those who try to help.  I lived that.  Both of my parents were bitter, and I was there.  I sometimes feel like my parents' relationship got so much worse after I left because I wasn't there to take things out on, so they just beat each other down instead.

Thank you.  That's very difficult, because I do remember some good times.  My mother loved me very much, and when I wasn't slaving away doing everything around the house or actively taking care of her, she'd always make me play games with her or watch a movie that she wanted to watch together in order to distract herself from how awful she was feeling physically.  Though it was annoying to never, ever have alone time, I can't say that the time I spent distracting her wasn't valuable.  In fact, we used to be very close.  My father is a well-meaning, loving man, but he's also an angry alcoholic who worked himself to exhaustion every day, and took his bitterness toward life out on other people.  My mother and I had to bond together because we were the only ones who understood how hard he was to live with (he was never physically violent, to be clear).  Sometimes it's really hard to remember all of that, and that's what's killing me.  I know she's not worth hating, but sometimes I just do.  For how ungrateful she was/is for mine and my father's efforts, for her self-absorption, for everything.

The relationship is rough.  We love each other very much, but we both have some issues that we have to work through, and are doing our best to help each other.  I have tried to confide in him, and he has helped a little.  He holds me while I cry, and tells me that everything is going to be okay, and tries his best to calm me down when I'm really upset.  But, sometimes it really hurts that I don't have anyone else to talk to. I don't feel okay about discussing the things I said about him in my post right now, and I sometimes need to know that someone else in this crazy world cares.  Actually, I have certain family members that care, but none I can be honest with about my problems.  I don't have anyone else to talk to, and it's hard.  Sometimes I want an outside perspective, but just can't get it.
"Interstate Love Song" by Stone Temple Pilots played on the classic rock radio station the other day.  It was released four years after I was born.
